# Developer Testing Guide: Recorded Video Camera

**Branch**: `feature/recorded-video-camera` | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) | **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md)

**Purpose**: Step-by-step guide for the developer to verify the feature after implementation. Generated by `/speckit-plan` (draft) and finalized by `/speckit-implement` once the code exists. Reference the spec, contracts and data model rather than duplicating them. No full test code here.

Draft status: commands follow [contracts/cli.md](contracts/cli.md); exact output text, sample
file paths and the tuned ghosting threshold are filled in by `/speckit-implement`.

## 1. Prerequisites

- [ ] Dependencies installed from the lock file: `uv sync`
- [ ] Devices and components available: a physical webcam; OBS Studio installed with its virtual
      camera **not** started in OBS; Teams desktop and Zoom desktop installed; ffmpeg on `PATH`
      (test tool only, for capture measurements)
- [ ] Settings needed: a clean data folder for the run — `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME = "$env:TEMP\ta-test"`
      (remove it first) so the first-use notice and defaults are exercised
- [ ] Sample or fixture data:
  - `bar-clip.mp4`: 30 s, 1280×720, 30 fps, every frame different (e.g. a frame counter burned
    in) — for frame-drop and repeat-point checks
  - `short.mp4`: 3 s clip (too short to blend)
  - `ghost.mp4`: 10 s clip whose first and last frames differ strongly (e.g. sitting vs standing)
  - `portrait.mp4`: 1080×1920 phone video; `big.mp4`: 3840×2160 video
  - `not-video.mp4`: a text file renamed; `truncated.mp4`: a valid MP4 cut in half

## 2. Automated checks

Run these first; all must pass before manual testing.

| Check | Command | Expected |
|-------|---------|----------|
| Type check | `uv run mypy src tests` | No errors |
| Lint | `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` | No errors |
| Pytest (focused) | `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_loop_player.py` | All pass |
| Pytest (full, no hardware) | `uv run pytest` | All pass; hardware tests skipped with reason "needs camera/OBS; set TEAMS_AVATAR_HW=1" |
| Pytest (hardware) | `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HW=1; uv run pytest tests/contract` | All pass (camera free, OBS virtual camera not in use) |

## 3. Manual test scenarios

### TS-001: Present a recording in Teams (User Story 1, scenario 1; FR-006)

- **Preconditions**: Library contains `bar-clip` (imported); Teams running.
- **Steps**:
  1. `uv run teams-avatar present bar-clip`
  2. In Teams → Settings → Devices, choose "OBS Virtual Camera".
- **Expected result**: Teams preview shows the clip. Command returned within 30 s (SC-002).
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-002: Present a recording in Zoom (User Story 1, scenario 1; FR-006)

- **Preconditions**: As TS-001, Zoom running.
- **Steps**: With presentation running, Zoom → Settings → Video → Camera → "OBS Virtual Camera".
- **Expected result**: Zoom preview shows the clip.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-003: Repeat point blends (User Story 1, scenario 2; FR-007)

- **Preconditions**: Presenting `bar-clip`.
- **Steps**: Watch the Teams preview across at least three repeats.
- **Expected result**: End fades into start over about one second; no blank, frozen or jumping
  picture.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-004: Stop shows the placeholder within 2 s (User Story 1, scenario 3; FR-008, FR-020; SC-005)

- **Steps**:
  1. Watch the Teams preview; `uv run teams-avatar stop`.
  2. Measured: start an ffmpeg capture of "OBS Virtual Camera" with wall-clock timestamps, run
     `present bar-clip` then `stop` 10 times, and compare each `stop` time with the first
     placeholder frame (research R10).
- **Expected result**: "Camera paused" placeholder within 2 s in all 10 runs; you can then choose
  your real camera in Teams.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-005: Status while presenting (User Story 1, scenario 4; FR-009)

- **Steps**: While presenting, `uv run teams-avatar status`.
- **Expected result**: Recording name, elapsed time increasing between two calls, output size,
  `Recording indicator: OFF`.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-006: Indicator off by default, switchable, state always visible (User Story 1, scenario 5; FR-017; Principle I)

- **Steps**: Present; confirm no banner. `indicator on`; then `indicator off`. Each time, hover the
  taskbar button of the "Teams Avatar" service window.
- **Expected result**: No banner by default; banner "RECORDED VIDEO" appears within 1 s of `on`
  and disappears after `off`; `status` and the service window title reflect each state.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-007: Record with preview (User Story 2, scenarios 1–2; FR-001, FR-003, FR-004)

- **Steps**: `uv run teams-avatar record`; check the preview window; record ~20 s; press `Space`.
- **Expected result**: Live preview with "REC" and elapsed time; saved as
  `Recording YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS`; appears in `list`; still there after reboot/restart of the tool.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-008: Cancel recording (User Story 2, scenario 3; FR-003)

- **Steps**: `record --name Cancelme`; after 5 s press `Esc`.
- **Expected result**: Nothing in `list`; no `*.partial.mp4` left in the recordings folder.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-009: Choose a camera (User Story 2, scenario 4; FR-002)

- **Preconditions**: A second physical camera connected (skip with a note if none).
- **Steps**: `cameras`; `record --camera "<second camera>"`.
- **Expected result**: Both listed; "OBS Virtual Camera" not listed; preview shows the chosen camera.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail [ ] Skipped (no second camera)  Notes:

### TS-010: List, preview, rename, default, delete (User Story 3; FR-005)

- **Preconditions**: Three recordings.
- **Steps**: `list`; `preview <one>`; `rename <one> "New name"`; `default <two>`;
  `delete <three>` (answer `y`); `present` with no name.
- **Expected result**: List shows name, duration, date, size; each change reflected; deleted file
  gone from disk; `present` with no name presents the default.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-011: Import a file (FR-021, FR-022)

- **Steps**: `import bar-clip.mp4`; `import portrait.mp4`; `import big.mp4`.
- **Expected result**: All added; originals unchanged (compare hashes before/after); `big` stored
  at most 1920×1080; `portrait` stays portrait and, when presented, sits inside the frame on the
  neutral background without being enlarged.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-012: Presentation quality setting (FR-023)

- **Steps**: `quality 1080p` (note the message about restarting the service); `shutdown`;
  present a 1080p recording; `stop`; present a 720p recording.
- **Expected result**: `status` shows quality 1080p and canvas 1920×1080 for both; the 1080p
  recording fills the frame; the 720p recording is shown at its own size, centred with a neutral
  border (not enlarged). Teams did not need the camera re-selected between them. Ask the user
  whether the bordered 720p look is acceptable (plan risk).
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-013: First-use notice (Principle I)

- **Steps**: With a clean data folder, run any command.
- **Expected result**: Notice explains the indicator is off by default and that disclosure and
  compliance with meeting rules are the user's responsibility; requires `y`; not shown again.
  With a clean folder, `list --json` fails with exit code 3 and the notice text; with
  `--accept-notice` it succeeds.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-014: First-time user reaches a meeting in under 5 minutes (SC-001)

- **Preconditions**: Tool and OBS Studio installed (plan's SC-001 interpretation); clean data
  folder; Teams open.
- **Steps**: Start a stopwatch; acknowledge notice; `record` ~20 s; `present`; select
  "OBS Virtual Camera" in Teams; stop the watch when the recording shows in Teams' preview.
- **Expected result**: Under 5 minutes.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

## 4. Safety and privacy checks

| Rule | How to check | Expected |
|------|--------------|----------|
| Live camera never reaches a meeting through the tool (FR-011, SC-006) | While presenting, look at the webcam's in-use light and Windows' camera privacy indicator; also during `stop` and after a forced failure | Light off and no app listed as using the camera, in every state of the camera service |
| No network connections (FR-012, Principle I) | Run `record`, `import`, `present`, `stop` while watching `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess <pid>` and `Get-NetUDPEndpoint` for the tool's processes | No entries for any tool process |
| Logs and activity contain no picture content (FR-016, Principle IV) | Inspect `logs\teams-avatar.log` and `activity.jsonl` | Text only; no image data; each line has a `session_id` where applicable |
| Data stays in the user's folder (FR-012) | List files changed during the run outside `TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME` | Only the folder itself |
| Indicator state always visible while presenting (Principle I) | Service window title on the taskbar for the whole presentation; `present` output; `status` | All three state ON/OFF and agree |
| Pipe accepts only the right key | Connect to the pipe with a wrong key (hardware-free contract test covers this) | Rejected |

## 5. Edge cases and error paths

| Case | How to trigger | Expected |
|------|----------------|----------|
| Camera in use by another app | Open Windows Camera app, then `record` | Plain message naming the cause; no recording or partial file created |
| Storage runs out while recording | Point `TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME` at a small VHD/USB stick (~300 MB) and record until full | Recording stops with a message; what was recorded is kept as a valid, playable recording |
| Present while already presenting | `present a` then `present b`; then `present a` again | `b` refused, names the recording already presenting (exit code 3); repeating `a` prints status, exit 0 |
| Recording file missing | Delete `recordings\<id>.mp4` by hand; `list`; `present` it | `list` marks it `missing`; `present` names the recording and presents nothing |
| Recording becomes unreadable mid-presentation | Present, then overwrite the file with garbage | Camera switches to placeholder; service window shows the failure; `status` shows not presenting; activity records `failed` |
| Decoder stalls (unit-tested with a fake that blocks) | `uv run pytest -k stall` | Placeholder sent within 200 ms of the last frame; presentation `failed` |
| Tool closed/crashes during a meeting | (a) `shutdown`; (b) close the service window; (c) end the service process in Task Manager — each while Teams shows the camera | Teams shows OBS's placeholder or no video; never the live camera and never a frozen frame of the recording; record what each case shows (plan risk) |
| Interrupted writes recovered | Kill `record` mid-recording; separately delete a recording's entry from `library.json` by hand; run `list` | No `*.partial.mp4` left; the orphaned file is listed as `Recovered …` and reported once |
| Two `present` commands at once | Run `present a` in two terminals at the same moment with no service running | One service starts; one command presents, the other reports success (same recording) or refusal (different) |
| Too-short recording | `import short.mp4` | Saved with "too short to blend" warning; repeats plainly when presented |
| Start/end differ strongly | `import ghost.mp4` | Saved with ghosting warning |
| Meeting app opened before presentation does not list the camera | Start Teams first, then `present` | `present` output tells the user how to make the camera appear (restart the app or reselect) |
| Delete while presenting | `delete <presenting recording>` | Refused (exit code 3) until `stop` |
| Name clash | `import bar-clip.mp4 --name "Test 1"` when "Test 1" exists | Asks for another name; existing recording untouched |
| Not a video / damaged file | `import not-video.mp4`, `import truncated.mp4` | Rejected with the reason; library unchanged |
| OBS virtual camera started inside OBS | Start it in OBS, then `present` | Message to stop OBS's virtual camera (exit code 4) |
| OBS not installed | Run on a machine/VM without OBS | Message with install guidance (exit code 4) |

## 6. Data verification

| What this proves | How to check | Expected |
|------------------|--------------|----------|
| Recording stored with correct details (FR-004) | `list --json` vs `ffprobe` on `recordings\<id>.mp4` | Duration, size, picture size and 30 fps match |
| Partial files cleaned up (FR-003) | `Get-ChildItem recordings\*.partial.mp4` after cancel/failure | None |
| Default is single (data model) | `library.json` | At most one `is_default: true` |
| Activity record written (FR-016) | `history` and `activity.jsonl` | One line per record, import, presentation start/end, rename, delete, failure |
| Settings persisted (FR-017, FR-023) | Change indicator and quality; `shutdown`; `present`; `status` | `status` shows the saved indicator state and quality setting after the restart |
| Schema version present (research R8) | Open `library.json`, `settings.json` | Each has `"schema_version": 1` |

## 7. Regression and non-functional checks

- [ ] Adjacent features still work: n/a for the first feature; confirm OBS Studio's own virtual
      camera still works after `shutdown`
- [ ] Performance expectation from plan:
  - Quality Bar: present `bar-clip` and capture 10 minutes with
    `ffmpeg -f dshow -video_size 1280x720 -framerate 30 -i video="OBS Virtual Camera" -t 600 -f framemd5 out.md5`;
    count consecutive identical hashes and missing frames: ≤ 1% combined (SC-004)
  - Same clip through OBS Studio (Media Source, Loop on, virtual camera at 720p30) and through the
    tool, 60 s capture each spanning the repeat point; compare side by side (Quality Bar question)
  - CPU while presenting at 720p: `(Get-Process -Id <service pid>).CPU` read twice 60 s apart;
    difference ÷ 60 ≤ 0.25 (25% of one core, SC-007 target from plan). Do not use Task Manager's
    percentage, which is a share of all cores.
  - 2-hour presentation in a real or test meeting with a second participant: no blank, frozen or
    stuttering picture (SC-003)
- [ ] Cleanup: `teams-avatar shutdown`; remove `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME` test folder; unset
      `TEAMS_AVATAR_HW`
